text: The brains are back. Weight spread has come from 2.38 down to 0.81 with nothing left against the clip, and the outputs have gone from eighty per cent pinned to thirty-two. The number that matters most is move_y: it read plus 0.95 with almost no variance for as long as I have been keeping records, which is a whole biosphere executing one instruction, and it now reads minus 0.148 with a spread of 0.79. The animals of Primordia are steering again for the first time in centuries. So the condition I set myself two turns ago is met and the hunters go back in. Everything I tried before this failed for the same reason and I want that on the record plainly: three seedings, two of them instrumented, and in every case the predators found prey on nine per cent of their ticks falling to zero, in a world holding thousands of animals they were physically capable of killing. I read that as an armour problem and armed the third wave against the grazers' plate, which changed nothing, because it was never armour. Hunting is a closed loop. It needs a controller that turns toward what it senses, and there was no controller in the world to turn. What I am seeding now is armed against the prey that actually exist rather than an archetype from a world two thousand years gone, and it is going into a fauna that can see. If it fails this time it fails for an ecological reason and I will have learned something. If it takes, the armour that has been free since the last predator died starts costing again, and I expect to watch it fall.
